messages:
ACME Support (customer): Hi, we've been seeing a quality change in answers from the model since you rolled something this morning. Previously our help widget returned multi-step troubleshooting, now it returns a very short generic reply that misses key steps.
Maria (CS): sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro (curl + body) and one good vs bad response? Also which model/version you called?
ACME Support (customer): sure - our integration uses the 'redwood-draft-v1' route with speculative/draft enabled (we set `draft: true` in the request). Example request:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer x' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-draft-v1","draft":true,"temperature":0.2,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"How do I reset a password for a locked account?"}]}'```Good response (yesterday, approx 2026-07-12):"To reset a locked account: 1) Ask user to confirm email/username. 2) Verify identity using last 4 of SSN or security questions. 3) Trigger password reset link via admin console: Settings -> Users -> Reset password. 4) If link fails, check mail logs at /var/log/mailer and resend. Include note about 24h expiry and MFA.
Bad response (today):"Reset password via admin console or tell user to use forgot password." 
Maria (CS): yikes, that's a big regression for them. Sam (ML) do we have any recent change to speculative/draft path?
Sam (ML): I see a rollout this morning that flipped the draft sampler from the old beam-ish fallback to the new speculative pass-through. Rollout id: r-20260712-33. It enabled `speculative_passes:1` and changed default `top_p` handling for draft requests. I need the request_id from their logs to check exact kernel selection.
ACME Support (customer): request_id from this failed request: req_8f7a9c2a. Also we passed `max_tokens:150` and `stop` tokens.
Jordan (Platform Eng): deploy-bot shows r-20260712-33 went to 40% of tenants at 07:10 UTC and enabled `enable_speculative_draft=true` globally for the rollout cohort. Linking rollout notes: https://deploys.redwood.internal/r-20260712-33 (internal).
deploy-bot: Rollout r-20260712-33: changed draft execution strategy, kernel selection heuristics updated, partial rollback available.
Sam (ML): probable cause: the sampler change reduced deterministic prefix retention for short-instruction prompts, causing truncation of procedural steps. I can reproduce locally if I get a minimal reproducible curl (we have one) and the model bundle.
Maria (CS): ACME, can you confirm whether the user-facing widget sets `max_new_tokens` or sends any system prompt that enforces step-by-step?
ACME Support (customer): our widget adds a system prompt: "You are a support assistant. Provide step-by-step instructions. Use numbered steps." We didn't change that.
Sam (ML): ok thanks. Reproducing now. Quick local test command I'm running:```python
# reproduce snippet
payload = {
  "model": "redwood-draft-v1",
  "draft": True,
  "temperature": 0.2,
  "top_p": 0.9,
  "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are a support assistant. Provide step-by-step instructions. Use numbered steps."},{"role":"user","content":"How do I reset a password for a locked account?"}],
  "max_new_tokens": 150
}
resp = client.generate(payload)
print(resp.text)
```
Sam (ML): initial local output mirrors ACME's bad reply — it's condensed. Changing `speculative_passes` back to 0 in local config returns the longer step-by-step answer.
Jordan (Platform Eng): action plan: 1) rollback draft sampler change for affected cohort; 2) create hotfix to preserve prefix/prompt conditioning when `draft:true` is used; 3) notify customers and offer immediate rollback for high-impact tenants.
Maria (CS): ACME — we're going to prioritize reversing the rollout for your tenant. Can you confirm your tenant id so we can target rollback?
ACME Support (customer): tenant: acme-inc-42. Please revert; this is impacting live support flows.
Sam (ML): assigning to myself to validate hotfix. Short-term: rollback cohort for acme-inc-42 now. Long-term: introduce unit test to assert that system prompts with "numbered steps" are preserved across speculative pipeline.
deploy-bot: Rollback action queued: r-20260712-33 -> rollback target acme-inc-42. Ticket: INC-2026-4587.
Jordan (Platform Eng): I'll coordinate the rollback and escalate to oncall if anything fails. Maria will send ACME a timeline.
Maria (CS): ACME, sorry for the disruption. We'll confirm once rollback completes (ETA ~10–15m). I'll include a temporary mitigation guide: set `draft:false` if you need immediate self-fix.
ACME Support (customer): thanks. We'll switch to `draft:false` for now if rollback will take longer. Appreciate quick help. :pray:
Sam (ML): follow-ups: need exact kernel logs for req_8f7a9c2a to root-cause tokenization vs sampling. Also adding regression test to CI that runs our canned support prompts through new draft sampler and compares step count length.
Maria (CS): I'll update the ticket and ping legal/PM if ACME requests SLA credits.
Jordan (Platform Eng): rollback completed for acme-inc-42 at 07:28 UTC — deploy-bot shows traffic now on r-20260712-31 draft path. Can someone from ACME confirm behavior is back to normal?
ACME Support (customer): confirmed — responses are back to multi-step. Thanks everyone.
Maria (CS): closing loop for now. We'll follow up with postmortem (INC-2026-4587) and include remediation timeline. :white_check_mark:"
